# Sirach Chapter 38 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_038_page_001.jpg

---

**38:1** Honor the physician with the honor due him, in view of your need of him, for the Lord created him;

**38:2** for healing comes from the Most High, and he will receive a gift from the king.

**38:3** The skill of the physician lifts up his head, and in the sight of great men he is admired.

**38:4** The Lord created medicines from the earth, and a sensible man will not despise them.

**38:5** Was not water made sweet with a piece of wood in order that he might make known to all men his power?

**38:6** And he gave skill to human beings in order that he might be glorified in his wondrous works.

**38:7** By them the physician cures and takes away pain, and the pharmacist makes a compound of them.

**38:8** There is no end to his works, and from him healing spreads over the whole earth.

**38:9** My son, when you are sick do not be negligent, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.

**38:10** Put aside your wrongdoing and direct your hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all sin.

**38:11** Give a sweet-smelling offering and a memorial of fine flour, and pour oil upon your offering, as one who is not yet dead.

**38:12** And give the physician his place, for the Lord created him too; do not let him leave you, for there is need of him.

**38:13** There is a time when success lies in the hands of physicians,

**38:14** for they too will pray to the Lord that he should grant them success in diagnosis and in healing, for the sake of preserving life.

**38:15** He who sins before his Maker, let him fall into the care of a physician.

**38:16** My son, let your tears fall over the dead; as one suffering greatly begin the lament; wrap the body in its shroud as is fitting; do not neglect his burial.

**38:17** Make bitter weeping and passionate lament; carry out the mourning as he deserves, for one day or two, to avoid censure; then be comforted for your grief.

**38:18** For grief may result in death, and the grief of the heart wears away strength.

**38:19** In calamity grief abides, and the life of the poor weighs down the heart.

**38:20** Do not give your heart to grief; drive it away; remember your own end.

**38:21** Do not forget — there is no returning; you cannot help him or yourself.

**38:22** "Remember my judgment, for yours will be the same: yesterday mine and today yours."

**38:23** When the dead is at rest, let his memory rest too; be comforted for him when his spirit has departed.

**38:24** The wisdom of a scribe depends on the opportunity of leisure; and he who has little business may become wise.

**38:25** How can he who holds the goad become wise, who glories in the shaft of a goad, who drives oxen, and is occupied with their labors, and whose talk is about bulls?

**38:26** He sets his heart on making a straight furrow, and he is anxious about fodder for the heifers.

**38:27** So too is every craftsman and master craftsman who works by night as well as by day; who cut seal designs; whose purpose is to make a faithful likeness; and who puts his heart into completing his work.

**38:28** So too is the smith sitting at his anvil; intent on his ironwork; the breath of fire melts his flesh, and he struggles with the heat of the furnace; the noise of the hammer deafens him; his eyes are on the pattern of the object; he sets his heart on completing his work, and he stays up to give it a finished appearance.

**38:29** So too is the potter, sitting at his work, and turning the wheel with his feet; he is continually anxious about his work, and each piece is produced by his craft.

**38:30** He fashions the clay with his arm, and bends its strength with his feet; he sets his heart on finishing the glazing, and he stays up to clean the kiln.

**38:31** All these trust to their hands, and each is skillful in his own work.

**38:32** Without them a city cannot be established, and men can neither sojourn nor live there.

**38:33** Yet they are not sought out for the council of the people, nor do they attain eminence in the public assembly. They do not sit in the judge's seat, nor do they understand the covenant of judgment; they cannot expound instruction and judgment, and they are not found using proverbs.

**38:34** But they keep stable the fabric of the world, and their prayer is in the practice of their trade.
